messages.subject: Difference between est.rf() and est.map()
parts:
I am having some trouble understanding the difference between these two functions.

Lets say we have an F2 population, and our markers are clustered and ordered. In the calculation of the genetic distances then, is it not simply a case of estimating the recombination fraction between markers using an EM algorithm, and then converting these rf values into cM distances using a mapping function such as Haldane or Kosambi?

This is obviously not the case, as the computation times for est.rf() and est.map() are drastically different. Why is this the case?

Thanks and best wishes
Alex

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Difference between est.rf() and est.map()
parts:
est.rf() looks at each pair of markers in isolation and seeks to estimate the recombination fraction between them.
In a backcross, it seems counts recombination events.
In an intercross, it needs to use an interative algorithm to deal with the het:het cases (which could be 0 or 2 recombinations).
In either case, any individual with a missing genotype at one or the other marker is omitted.

est.map() considers all the markers on a chromosome, one chromosome at a time, and uses a hidden Markov model to estimate the inter-marker distances, jointly. It uses data on all individuals including those with missing genotypes, and uses a model that accommodates genotyping error.

karl
